concepts.title: Objectives and Limitations of the Trial Balance

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Objectives and Limitations of the Trial Balance' refers to.
questions.a: The trial balance ascertains the arithmetical accuracy of ledger accounts, helps in locating errors, and provides the basis for preparing final accounts; yet errors of principle, complete omission and compensating errors do not disturb its agreement.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Objectives and Limitations of the Trial Balance'.
questions.a: A tallied trial balance is only a presumption of accuracy, since several classes of errors leave the two sides equal.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Objectives and Limitations of the Trial Balance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 6.2 Objectives of Preparing the Trial Balance (source: keac106.txt sections 6.2, 6.2.1, 6.2.2)

concepts.title: Classification of Errors: Omission, Commission, Principle and Compensating

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Classification of Errors: Omission, Commission, Principle and Compensating' refers to.
questions.a: Accounting errors are classified as errors of complete or partial omission, errors of commission such as wrong posting or casting, errors of principle that break the accounting rules, and compensating errors that cancel one another.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Classification of Errors: Omission, Commission, Principle and Compensating'.
questions.a: Classifying an error first decides whether it can be rectified through the suspense account or needs a correcting journal entry.
